collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: We lose calls after hours,Calls going to voicemail
collected_dynamic_variables.call_volume: About 15 missed calls a week go to voicemail

transcript:
User: Hi, I saw your ad about missed calls. We lose calls after hours and I'm curious how it works.
Agent: Got it, thanks for calling in — a lot of folks click that ad for the same reason.  

So when you say “we lose calls after hours,” what actually happens to those calls right now — do they hit voicemail, an answering service, or just ring out?
User: They typically go to voicemail.
Agent: Gotcha, so most after-hours calls are just landing in voicemail.  

Do people actually leave many messages, or do you feel like a lot of them just hang up and probably call the next place?
User: Most hang up, but about 15 missed calls a week go to voicemail.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense — if they hit voicemail, most people just move on.  

So roughly 15 people a week are getting pushed to voicemail after hours… what kind of business are you running?
User: I run an auto repair shop called 'Precision Auto Care' in Austin, TX.
Agent: Nice, I know that type of shop really lives and dies by the phones.  

When those 15 or so calls a week hit voicemail at Precision Auto Care, what do you feel you’re missing most — bigger repair jobs, emergency tow-ins, or just a steady stream of new customers?
User: Mainly a steady stream of new customers, since around 60% would book if someone answered.
Agent: Got it, so most of those after-hours calls could turn into brand‑new customers if someone just picked up.  

Mhm… for those new customers at your shop, what’s a typical first ticket worth on average — are we talking more like $300, $600, $800 for that first visit?
User: The average job value for a first visit is about $450.
Agent: Perfect, that helps. So with your numbers, those after‑hours voicemails are bleeding out around seventeen‑and‑a‑half grand a month in work that could’ve booked if someone just picked up.  

So… to walk you through how we plug that leak and show you your exact numbers, would you be open to a quick 20‑minute walkthrough this week — is later today or tomorrow better?
User: Yes, I'm open to a walkthrough. Tomorrow would be better.
Agent: Nice, tomorrow works.  

Quickly so I can get this set up right — what’s your first name?
User: I'm not sharing my name yet, just interested in the service for 'Precision Auto Care'. What's next?
Agent: Totally fine, I hear you — we can keep it high‑level for now.  

So, next step: after hours, instead of callers hitting voicemail, our system answers, talks to them, and books the appointment or takes a firm callback request so you don’t lose the job — do you want to focus more on after‑hours only, or also times when your front desk is slammed during the day?
User: We'd focus more on after-hours only, when calls typically go to voicemail.
Agent: Makes sense, after‑hours is usually where the money leaks the fastest.  

So instead of voicemail, our system would answer in your shop’s name, grab the caller’s info, and either book the appointment into your calendar or lock in a callback window for your team the next morning — would you want it to actually book into a schedule, or just capture name/number and what they need?
User: I’d prefer it to actually book into a schedule for more efficient appointment handling.
Agent: Got it, you want it actually booking into your schedule so those after‑hours calls turn into real appointments, not just messages.  

So… what do you use today for scheduling at Precision Auto Care — something like Shopmonkey, Tekmetric, Mitchell, Google Calendar, or something else?
User: We use Google Calendar for scheduling at Precision Auto Care.
Agent: Nice, that actually makes things simpler — we can book straight into a dedicated Google Calendar for your shop’s appointments.  

Since you’re just exploring right now, would it be helpful if I walked you through, step‑by‑step, what a typical after‑hours caller would experience with our system instead of voicemail?
User: Yes, a walkthrough of what an after-hours caller would experience with your system sounds helpful.
Agent: Cool, let’s keep it super simple and concrete.  

So… say someone calls Precision Auto Care at 8:45pm with a car issue — do you want them to be able to (A) pick a specific appointment time, or (B) choose a general window like “tomorrow morning / afternoon”?
User: I'd prefer if they could pick a specific appointment time.
Agent: Perfect, that’s exactly what we’re built for.  

So here’s how it plays out after hours: caller dials Precision Auto Care, they hear a professional greeting in your shop’s name, it asks a couple quick questions about the car and the issue, then offers real open times from your Google Calendar (like “Tomorrow at 9:30, 11:00, or 2:15, which works best?”) and books it under their name — does that flow line up with how you like to schedule now, or would you tweak anything in that script?
User: That flow sounds good as is, aligns well with our current scheduling process.
Agent: Nice, that makes it easy to plug in without changing how you work.  

Since you’re liking the flow, do you want to keep this as an after‑hours only setup for now, or are you at all curious what it could do during busy daytime spikes too?
User: For now, let's focus on after-hours. But I'm open to exploring daytime options in the future.
Agent: That totally works — most shops start after‑hours and expand once they see it booking real jobs.  

Since you’re serious enough to be thinking “after‑hours only,” would you be open to a short live walkthrough with Jay so he can show you exactly how it plugs into your Google Calendar and what your callers would hear?
User: Yes, I'm open to a live walkthrough to see how it integrates with our system and benefits our callers.
Agent: Nice, that’s exactly what Jay can show you.  

Quick thing so we can line that up properly later—what time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: I'm in Central Time, here in Austin, TX.
Agent: Got it, Central time in Austin.  

And just to confirm for later, is the number you’re calling from now the best one to text a walkthrough confirmation to?
User: No, the best contact number for the walkthrough confirmation is +15123120001.
Agent: Got it, we’ll use +1 512‑312‑0001 as the best number for the walkthrough confirmation.  

Since we don’t have your name yet, when Jay calls or texts that number, what should he ask for—just “the owner at Precision Auto Care,” or something else you prefer?
User: Yes, asking for "the owner at Precision Auto Care" is perfect for the walkthrough confirmation.
Agent: Perfect, we’ll have Jay ask for “the owner at Precision Auto Care” on that number.  

Since you don’t want to share your name yet, do you still want to lock in a specific day and time with him now, or would you rather just wait for a text first and book it from there?
User: Let's lock in a specific day and time for the live call now.
Agent: Makes sense, let’s lock it in while we’re here.  

Since you’re in Central time, what works better for you for a 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay—tomorrow late morning or later in the afternoon?
User: Tomorrow late morning works better for me. Could we book it for then?
Agent: Nice, we’ve got some room tomorrow late morning.  

I can get you in at either 11:30 or 12:15 Central — which works better for your 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay?
User: Let's go with 11:30 Central for the walkthrough. Yes, book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: You’re all set — I’ve got you booked for tomorrow at 11:30 Central with Jay. You’ll get a text confirmation shortly at that 512 number with the details and a link in case you need to reschedule.

Is there anything else you want to know before that walkthrough?

Alright, really glad you called in today. Jay’s looking forward to showing you how we can stop those after‑hours calls from turning into lost jobs. Have a great rest of your day, talk soon — bye!
